notes:
Pages: 9 (budget up to 9): Soviet Union, Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, Eastern Front (World War II), Soviet-Japanese War, Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran, Tuvan People's Republic, Dissolution of the Soviet Union (three reads, the text cut off in July 1990), Occupation of the Baltic states, Far Eastern Republic. The general Soviet Union page proved thin on dates, so shapes 1953-1987 rest on the general page and are 'unverified: page budget' for their borders.

What Cliopatria's USSR row gets wrong, shape by shape: (1) Xinjiang (5,487 cells) is inside the 1940-1942 shapes: no page shows Soviet rule there; removed, to be examined by a gap-filler with 'Sheng Shicai' and 'Xinjiang under Soviet influence'. (2) Occupied or satellite states drawn as Soviet land: northern Iran 1942-46, Poland to 1952, the Soviet zone of Germany to 1948, Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia and Austria in 1945-46, Manchuria, Inner Mongolia and northern Korea 1946-47, Czechoslovakia 1969-1990, Afghanistan 1979-1989; all removed from the corrected shapes and drawn, where a page supports it, by occupation events (Iran, Manchuria, Korea, Afghanistan), otherwise by a single confidence-1 occupation pair for Eastern Europe and the German zone. The Eastern Bloc states are sovereign states with their own dossiers (Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Romania, the GDR) and are not drawn as Soviet vassals. (3) Lakes: the shapes of 1932-1972 and 1976-1991 have holes for Baikal, Balkhash, Issyk-Kul, the Aral Sea, Onega and Ladoga; the corrections add the gazetteer's lake cells, which leaves a rim of about 340 cells (200 of them round the Aral Sea) unfilled. (4) Lithuania leaves Cliopatria's shape in 1990 but the Soviet government recognised it only on 6 September 1991: kept as contested. (5) The Far East is missing in 1922-23 although the Far Eastern Republic was absorbed in November 1922. (6) Tuva is inside every shape although the Tuvan People's Republic was a satellite until 1944: drawn as a vassal instead.

Not settled, for the reviewer: (a) the ruler strip: no page I could read lists the Soviet leaders; omitted. (b) Pages did not date: the incorporation of eastern Poland (November 1939), the Moscow Peace Treaty day, Petsamo, Carpathian Ruthenia, Kaliningrad, the Franz Josef Land annexation, the end of the Soviet occupation of Eastern Europe (1947), of Germany (1949) and of Korea (1948), and the Ayano-Maysky pocket (June 1923, Priamurye dossier). (c) The Paris peace treaties of 1947, the Potsdam arrangements, the 1954 transfer of Crimea and the Karelo-Finnish SSR's 1956 abolition were not on the pages. (d) Port Arthur and Dalian (Soviet 'preeminent interests'), the Hanko lease, Salla and Kuusamo are not placed. (e) The Estonian and Latvian border strips given to the RSFSR in 1944-45 (Pechory, Abrene) are in the RSFSR dossier, not here. (f) Cliopatria's 1941 shape ignores the 1941 invasion; the ledger carries it. (g) The 1990-91 declarations of other republics (Armenia 23 August 1990, Ukraine's sovereignty 16 July 1990) are not territorial and are not recorded. (h) 'mujahideen' is the counterpart name for the Afghan resistance in the war entry; 'mengjiang' and 'Soviet-occupied Central and Eastern Europe' are not dossiers.

Gazetteer: Franz Josef Land is not a gazetteer region (used as a real name); Petsamo and the Karelian Isthmus are placed by Nikel and Vyborg radii.
